modelResponse.episodeSummary: 64yo female, 1:1 Atrial Flutter with wide QRS, critical severity, borderline hypotensive (BP 88/54).
modelResponse.rhythm: 1:1 Atrial Flutter with Flecainide-induced QRS widening
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Wide bizarre QRS not conforming to typical RBBB or LBBB pattern; 1:1 AV conduction
pWavePresent: false (flutter waves faintly visible distorting ST segments in V1)
modelResponse.mechanism: Flecainide (a Class IC antiarrhythmic) slows atrial conduction, which can convert atrial fibrillation into atrial flutter. Simultaneously, it slows AV nodal conduction; however, if the AV node is not sufficiently blocked (no co-prescribed AV nodal blocker), the slowed atrial rate may paradoxically allow 1:1 AV conduction. The drug also slows ventricular conduction, resulting in the observed wide QRS complex (180 ms vs baseline 88 ms).
contributingFactors: Lack of co-prescribed AV nodal blocker (e.g., beta-blocker or CCB) with flecainide therapy
Recent initiation of flecainide 100 mg BID (2 weeks ago)

rejectedAlternatives.why: Atrial rate is 200 bpm matching ventricular rate, and morphology shows flutter waves in V1; patient has no structural heart disease (normal echo 3 weeks ago).
The specific combination of flecainide use, 1:1 conduction at 200 bpm, and the bizarre QRS widening is pathognomonic for Class IC induced flutter.

recommendedActions: Immediate synchronized cardioversion (due to borderline hypotension BP 88/54 and critical rate)
Administer IV beta-blocker or non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker to slow AV conduction
Continuous cardiac monitoring and frequent BP checks
